articles.title: Incoming Democrats plan to challenge Trump's tariff powers.
p: Incoming Democrats in Congress plan to take action against President Trump's power to set tariffs.
Hakeem Jeffries has promised to act against tariffs that are raising prices for Americans.
Ron Wyden also plans to restore the authority of Congress over trade policy.
Some Republicans have also said that tariffs have made goods too expensive.
Trump could announce new duties on imports from more than twelve economies.
Such a move could increase costs for businesses that depend on imported products or materials.
Consumers may then have to pay higher prices.
Businesses and families also face continued uncertainty because they do not know how much future imports will cost.
Tariffs have already contributed to U.S. consumer-price inflation, which has reached an annual rate of 3.7%.
However, changing the policy may not bring quick results.
Existing tariffs could be difficult to remove in a short period, even if Congress takes action.
Congressional action after January could reshape U.S. trade policy and reduce the president's control over tariffs.
The dispute is also important outside the United States.
It could affect global suppliers, product prices and trade negotiations between countries.
Companies that sell goods to the United States may need to prepare for higher duties or changing rules.
The final result will depend on what Trump announces and how Congress responds.

quiz.why: The text states that annual U.S. consumer-price inflation has reached 3.7%.

o: They do not know future import costs
quiz.why: Future tariff decisions could change the cost of imported goods and materials.

articles.title: Technology shares lifted the market on Friday after a difficult week.
p: US stocks ended Friday with mixed results after losses earlier in the week.
The S&P 500, a broad measure of large US companies, rose 0.31% to 7,376.86.
The technology-heavy Nasdaq gained 1.09%, but the Dow fell 0.46%.
For November 2–6, the S&P 500 lost 2.68%, the Nasdaq dropped 3.37%, and the Dow declined 0.94%.
Shares linked to artificial intelligence, or AI, recovered after Thursday's severe technology sell-off.
Hospitals and liquor companies exposed to tariffs also gained after the Democrats' election victory.
Several economic and policy facts shaped trading.
Employers added 165,000 jobs in October, much more than the expected 59,000.
Unemployment fell from 4.2% to 4.1%.
These figures showed strength in the job market.
The Fed kept its policy interest-rate range at 3.75%–4.00% after its October decision.
Markets put the chance of a December rate increase at 76.8% on November 6.
The ten-year Treasury yield, the return paid on long-term US government debt, was near 4.86%.
Political results affected industries in different ways.
Defense shares fell between 4% and 12% after the midterm election.
In contrast, alcohol companies affected by tariffs rose because of hopes for policy relief.
Tariffs are taxes placed on imported goods.
The moves showed that investors were changing their views about which companies could benefit from policy after the election.
Fear eased, but it remained important.
The VIX, an index that measures expected stock-market changes and is often called a fear gauge, closed near 25.64 on November 6, down from 28.18.
Investors also rotated toward Berkshire as AI shares weakened.
Rotation means moving money from one type of investment into another.
This shift suggested that some investors were looking beyond AI-linked companies during the period of weakness.
The Magnificent Seven gave mixed signals.
These seven large technology-related companies represented about 34% of the S&P 500's value, so their moves had a strong effect.
Nvidia rose 2.78% on Friday after collapsing 9.26% on Thursday.
Tesla gained 4.23% Friday, although it had fallen 10.1% after the election.
Alphabet and Meta each rose about 0.8%.
Amazon slipped about 0.3%, Microsoft fell 0.99% amid reports of lower neocloud usage, and Apple recorded a modest decline.
Investors next face several economic reports and company results.
October CPI, which measures changes in consumer prices, arrives Tuesday, November 10, before the Fed's December meeting.
Weekly jobless claims and existing-home sales are due Thursday, November 12.
October producer prices, which measure prices received by producers, arrive Friday, November 13.
CoreWeave reports results Tuesday, while Cisco and Applied Materials report Thursday.
Overall, Friday's technology rebound moved the market most because the Nasdaq rose 1.09%, more than the S&P 500, while AI-linked shares recovered.
Gains in Nvidia and Tesla supported that move.
However, the Dow's decline, the week's losses, high Treasury yields, and the strong probability of a December rate increase limited the positive picture.
Election effects and lower fear also mattered, but their impact was less broad than the recovery in major technology shares.

words.d: A period when many investors sell shares and prices fall quickly.
The upper and lower limits set for an important borrowing rate.
The return paid to an investor who owns US government debt.
A tax placed on goods imported from another country.
A measure of how much change or worry investors expect in the stock market.
The movement of investment money from one market group to another.

quiz.q: Which major index gained the most on Friday?
quiz.why: The Nasdaq rose 1.09%, compared with a 0.31% gain for the S&P 500 and a decline for the Dow.

quiz.q: What happened to US unemployment in October?
quiz.why: The unemployment rate decreased from 4.2% to 4.1% in October.

quiz.q: Why did tariff-exposed alcohol companies rise?
quiz.why: The companies gained because the election result created hopes for relief from tariff policy.

quiz.q: Which upcoming report measures changes in consumer prices?
quiz.why: CPI measures changes in prices paid by consumers and is due on Tuesday, November 10.

articles.title: Real Madrid beat Valencia 3-0 at Mestalla.
p: Real Madrid defeated Valencia 3-0 at Mestalla on November 7.
The result gave Real Madrid their eighth victory in a row.
The team reached 30 points after playing 12 league matches.
Valencia ended the match with only ten players after José Gayà was dismissed.
Federico Valverde opened the scoring for Real Madrid in the 28th minute.
Eight minutes later, Arda Güler added the second goal.
The young attacking midfielder scored with his right foot from inside the penalty area.
His goal gave Real Madrid a 2-0 lead in the 36th minute.
Güler also played an important part in the third goal.
In the 75th minute, he assisted Kylian Mbappé, who completed the 3-0 result.
It was another successful match for Mbappé, as he scored for the seventh consecutive game.
Güler stayed on the field for nine more minutes before leaving the match in the 84th minute.
The game was a strong result for Real Madrid before the international break.
Güler started in attacking midfield, scored one goal and created another.
Valverde, Güler and Mbappé were the three goalscorers at Mestalla.
Real Madrid and Güler will now enter the international break after extending the club's winning run and improving their league points total.

one after another without a break
scored the first goal of a match
the large box near the goal on a football field

quiz.why: Real Madrid defeated Valencia 3-0 at Mestalla.

quiz.q: Who scored Real Madrid's first goal?
quiz.why: Valverde opened the scoring in the 28th minute.

quiz.q: How did Güler help with the third goal?
o: He scored with his left foot
quiz.why: Güler assisted Mbappé's goal in the 75th minute.

quiz.q: Why did Valencia finish with ten players?
quiz.why: Valencia had ten players at the end after Gayà's dismissal.

articles.title: Countries meet in Türkiye for COP31 climate talks.
p: Climate talks begin on Monday in Antalya, Türkiye, as nearly 190 countries are expected to take part in COP31.
The conference runs from November 9 through November 20.
Türkiye is hosting the meeting and holds its presidency, while Australia is leading the formal negotiations.
Delegates will discuss how countries can cut emissions and provide climate finance.
Support for adaptation in vulnerable countries remains a major issue.
These countries need help to prepare for and respond to the effects of climate change.
A leaders' summit is also planned for November 11 and 12.
The United Nations has warned that current national pledges could lead to roughly 2.6°C of warming.
This warning adds pressure on negotiators to make practical and visible progress.
However, dependence on fossil fuels makes the conference's objectives more difficult to reach.
Many countries still use these fuels as an important part of their energy systems.
The discussions are expected to continue until the final day of the conference.
Negotiators will work toward a closing agreement on November 20.
The outcome will show whether participating countries can move closer to stronger emissions cuts, better climate finance, and more adaptation support.
Delegates face the challenge of finding common positions among nearly 190 countries while also producing results that people can clearly see.

words.d: reductions in gases released into the air that cause climate change
money used to help countries deal with climate change
changes made to prepare for the effects of climate change
likely to be harmed or affected by something
serious promises to do something
fuels such as coal, oil, and natural gas

quiz.why: Türkiye is hosting COP31 in the city of Antalya.

quiz.q: Which country is leading the formal negotiations?
quiz.why: Australia is responsible for leading the formal negotiations at the conference.

quiz.q: What warming level could current pledges produce, according to the United Nations?
quiz.why: The United Nations warns that present pledges imply roughly 2.6°C of warming.

quiz.q: When is the closing agreement expected?
quiz.why: The talks continue until a closing agreement on November 20.
